name: Dark Viridian Green
lede: Dark Viridian Green is a deep, saturated blue-green, Robert Ridgway's darker step down from his own Viridian Green, built on the pigment name viridian.

sections.title: A pigment's name, one shade darker
sections.body: Ridgway placed Dark Viridian Green on plate VII in 1912, hue 37, tone k, directly below [[viridian-green|Viridian Green]] on the same card, itself built on the pigment name [[viridian]] [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary filed this darker name again in 1955, block 145, as a moderate green [2]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also lists a near-duplicate under a separate name, Spearmint Too, first recorded in 1917 [3]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[generic-viridian]] and [[arsenate]], both almost the same at 2.5 to 2.7 CIEDE2000 units [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green, as photographed, in only 8 of 23,781 paintings, 0.03 percent, rarer than 77 percent of the named colors we track [5]. The earliest dated match is an 1885 painting by Auguste Renoir; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [5]. With so few matches, no century or painter stands out against the archive's own baseline [5].
